content:
Formula: Integration by Parts
Exact Expression: \int u \, dv = uv - \int v \, du
Definitions: Theorem that transforms the integral of a product of functions into a potentially simpler integral.
Derivation/Reference: Integration of the product rule differential d(uv) = u dv + v du; Brook Taylor (1715)
Example: int x*e^x dx: let u=x, dv=e^x dx -> du=dx, v=e^x -> x*e^x - int e^x dx = x*e^x - e^x + C
Domain: integral_calculus
Assumptions: u and v have continuous derivatives on integration domain
Common Errors: Incorrect assignment of u and dv causing circular or escalating complexity
subject: Integration by Parts
